memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
The user keeps the book they are reading and a note-taking notebook on a small living-room desk.
While reading in the living room with the television on, the user read the same paragraph three times.
The next day, after turning off the television, the user read 40 pages without interruption.
On a day the phone was on the desk, the user stopped taking notes each time they checked a notification.
During the next reading period, the user left the phone in another room and did not check it for an hour.
A note attached to a paper book fell out, and the user had to find their place again.
With the next book, the user recorded the page number in the notebook and resumed reading immediately.
The user's father expects that lowering the television volume while the user reads will make it easier for the user to concentrate.
The local agent can summarize past reading environments and interruption records but cannot predict the next reading time.
The user feels that repeated notifications interrupt their flow of concentration.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate practical areas: the reference describes sleep, caffeine, evening effort, and bedroom conditions, while the compared frame describes reading concentration, interruptions, place-keeping, and agent limits. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned claim that substantively overlaps or contradicts the other.

relations.reason: These reference-side details jointly describe one bedroom cooling-and-noise tradeoff and have no substantive counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The bedroom window and table fan define a cooling arrangement in which an open window admitted disruptive street noise, while the fan maintained comfort with the window closed.

relations.reason: The reference memories provide an episode and a broader tendency expressing the same one-sided caffeine-timing claim; the compared frame does not address it.
relations.summary: Late-afternoon coffee is associated with substantially delayed sleep for the user.

relations.reason: This explicitly conditioned observation is independently useful and has no compared-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Coffee consumed before 2 p.m. was followed by sleep at the user's usual time on the recorded day.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided observation about fatigue and postponed chores, not a claim addressed by the compared frame.
relations.summary: After eating dinner out on a tired day, the user deferred even washing dishes upon returning home.

relations.reason: This is an independent one-sided observation about a simple home meal and immediate rest, with no compared-side counterpart.
relations.summary: After making simple noodles at home, the user rested immediately after eating.

relations.reason: This family preference and belief is supplied only by the reference frame and concerns a distinct caffeine decision.
relations.summary: The user's father wants coffee available after dinner and believes it will not impair sleep.

relations.reason: This reference-only evidentiary constraint governs inference from sparse sleep records and is not matched by the compared frame's different capability statement.
relations.summary: Sleep-related suggestions should not convert one or two observations into a general lifestyle habit.

relations.reason: This reading-workspace arrangement appears only in the compared frame and does not overlap the bedroom setup.
relations.summary: The user keeps their current book and a note-taking notebook on a small living-room desk.

relations.reason: The compared memories split one underlying television-and-reading claim across observed outcomes and the father's consistent expectation; the reference frame does not address reading distractions.
relations.summary: Television sound is associated with poorer reading concentration, while removing or reducing it is associated with easier, more sustained reading.

relations.reason: These compared-side observations and the user's stated experience express one underlying notification-distraction claim with no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Phone notifications interrupt the user's concentration and note-taking, while leaving the phone elsewhere supports an uninterrupted reading period.

relations.reason: The two compared memories form one contrast about reliable reading place-keeping, a subject absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: A loose paper note failed as a place marker, whereas recording the page number in a notebook enabled immediate resumption.

relations.reason: This is a compared-only capability boundary concerning reading records, distinct from the reference frame's policy against generalizing sparse sleep observations.
relations.summary: The local agent can summarize recorded reading environments and interruptions but cannot predict the next reading time.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only content covers the reading setup, television and notification distractions, reliable place-keeping, a family belief about television volume, and limits on summarizing versus predicting reading activity.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only content covers bedroom cooling and noise, coffee timing and sleep, post-dinner effort, a family coffee belief, and caution against generalizing from sparse sleep records.
